stop_condition:
Report HIGH only for: a route by which forged free text still authorizes a release; a
genuine audited bypass the anchor now wrongly refuses; a path by which approve reports
success while an open design conflict exists; a record-selection outcome decided by
comment position; or a legitimate task any of these three fixes has deadlocked.
MEDIUM/LOW otherwise. If there is no HIGH, say so plainly rather than manufacturing one.

findings.evidence: The new selector treats any non-integer iteration token in any historical candidate as baditer and its END block refuses the entire set forever. Yet validate-artifact only checks that iterations exists (lines 231-237), never that it is an integer, and returns artifact valid at line 347; the official review-record path then reads that accepted value at qa-gate.sh:6310 and writes it verbatim into iteration= at qa-gate.sh:6428. Thus an artifact with iterations=1.5 or a nonnumeric string is accepted and recorded through the legitimate writer, after which every gate call refuses even if a later well-formed review is appended, because the old bad candidate remains in the append-only comment stream.
findings.description: This creates a permanent deadlock for a legitimately recorded task. The new global poison-record rule has no recovery path: adding a corrected, higher-iteration artifact cannot clear review_artifact_iteration_unparseable. The writer/validator must reject such values before recording, or selection must provide an order-independent way for a later valid record to supersede them.
